**On-screen content:**
The instructor writes out the backtracking stubs for derangements:
- `is_a_solution(a, k, n)`: checks if $k == n$.
- `process_solution(a, k)`: prints the array.
- `construct_candidates(a, k, n, c, nc)`: generates integers from $1$ to $n$ excluding already used elements and excluding the current index $i$.

```c
// Conceptual candidate generation for derangements
void construct_candidates(int a[], int k, int n, int c[], int *nc) {
    bool in_perm[NMAX];
    for (int i = 1; i <= n; i++) in_perm[i] = false;
    for (int i = 1; i < k; i++) in_perm[a[i]] = true;

    *nc = 0;
    for (int i = 1; i <= n; i++) {
        if (!in_perm[i] && i != k) {
            c[*nc] = i;
            (*nc)++;
        }
    }
}
```

**On-screen content:** 
- Slide showing C code for `construct_candidates`.

![code: Candidate Constructor for Eight Queens in C](video-frame://63@42:38)

```c
void construct_candidates(int a[], int k, int n, int c[], int *ncandidates) {
    int i, j;
    bool legal_move;
    *ncandidates = 0;
    for (i = 1; i <= n; i++) {
        legal_move = true;
        for (j = 1; j < k; j++) {
            if (abs(k - j) == abs(i - a[j])) {
                legal_move = false; /* diagonal threat */
            }
            if (i == a[j]) {
                legal_move = false; /* column threat */
            }
        }
        if (legal_move) {
            c[*ncandidates] = i;
            (*ncandidates)++;
        }
    }
}
```
